title: 2015 AMC 10B Problem 25
statement: A rectangular box measures \(a \times b \times c,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are integers and \[1\leq a \leq b \leq c.\] The volume and the surface area of the box are numerically equal. How many ordered triples \((a,b,c)\) are possible?

solutions.text:
The condition is \[abc=2(ab+ac+bc).\] Since \(abc\le6bc\), we have \(a\le6\). Also \(a=1\) and \(a=2\) give no positive solutions, so test \(a=3,4,5,6\).

For \(a=3\), \((b-6)(c-6)=36\), giving \((b,c)=(7,42),\) \((8,24),\) \((9,18),\) \((10,15),\) \((12,12)\). For \(a=4\), \((b-4)(c-4)=16\), giving \((5,20),(6,12),(8,8)\).

For \(a=5\), \((3b-10)(3c-10)=100\), and the only solution with \(a\le b\le c\) is \((b,c)=(5,10)\). For \(a=6\), \((b-3)(c-3)=9\), and the only solution with \(a\le b\le c\) is \((6,6)\).

The total number of triples is \(5+3+1+1=10\).

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Fix \(a\le6\) and factor the remaining equation
